original_question: Let X be a Calabi-Yau threefold given as a complete intersection of one cubic hypersurface and two quadric hypersurfaces in P^6. Is it possible to prove a stronger Bogomolov inequality for slope-semistable torsion-free sheaves on X, analogous to the inequalities proved in the cited quintic and quadric-quartic cases, in a way that implies inequality (4.5)?
target_in_paper: Question 5.12 in Section 5.3 (Tilt stability): the open problem asking whether one can prove a stronger Bogomolov inequality for slope semistable torsion-free sheaves on the (3,2,2) complete intersection in P^6 so as to imply (5.5). ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s12215-022-00796-x.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the right geometric case (the complete intersection of one cubic and two quadrics in P^6), the right class of sheaves (slope-semistable torsion-free sheaves), the right comparison results (the quintic and quadric-quartic complete-intersection cases cited immediately before the question), and the right intended goal: obtaining a stronger Bogomolov inequality strong enough to imply the generalized inequality used for tilt stability. Calling this case Calabi-Yau is consistent with the surrounding sentence, although the formal question itself is stated just in terms of the complete-intersection description. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s12215-022-00796-x.pdf))
missing_details: The exact target is Question 5.12 in Section 5.3, not Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, or Theorem 1.3 from the introduction. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s12215-022-00796-x.pdf))
The referenced consequence is inequality (5.5), not (4.5). ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s12215-022-00796-x.pdf))

For a fully stand-alone version, X should be stated as a smooth projective polarized threefold; smoothness is implicit in the Section 5.3 setup. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s12215-022-00796-x.pdf))
The paper's ambient convention is that varieties are defined over an algebraically closed field K. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s12215-022-00796-x.pdf))

Slope semistability should be specified with respect to the polarization H = O_X(1), i.e. the hyperplane class induced from the embedding X ⊂ P^6. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s12215-022-00796-x.pdf))

To make 'implies (5.5)' self-contained, one should name the tilt-stability conditions sigma_{s,q} = (Coh^s(X), Z_{s,q}) and the parameter region Delta = {(s,q) in R^2 : q > s^2/2}. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s12215-022-00796-x.pdf))

The quadratic form Delta_H(E) appearing in (5.5) should be defined explicitly as (H^2 ch_1(E))^2 - 2(H^3 ch_0(E))(H ch_2(E)) in dimension 3. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12215-022-00796-x))

The twisted Chern characters in (5.5) should be written explicitly: ch_1^s(E) = ch_1(E) - sH ch_0(E), ch_2^s(E) = ch_2(E) - sH ch_1(E) + (s^2/2)H^2 ch_0(E), and ch_3^s(E) = ch_3(E) - sH ch_2(E) + (s^2/2)H^2 ch_1(E) - (s^3/6)H^3 ch_0(E). ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12215-022-00796-x))

The comparison results are cited precisely as [96, Theorem 1.1] for the quintic threefold and [103, Proposition 1.1] for the complete intersection of a quadric and a quartic in P^5. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s12215-022-00796-x.pdf))
refined_question: Let K be an algebraically closed field, let X ⊂ P^6_K be a smooth complete intersection of type (3,2,2), and let H = O_X(1). Can one prove, for H-slope-semistable torsion-free sheaves on X, a stronger Bogomolov inequality of the same kind as in [96, Theorem 1.1] and [103, Proposition 1.1], strong enough to imply that whenever an object E in D^b(X) is sigma_{s,q}-semistable for some (s,q) in Delta = {(s,q) in R^2 : q > s^2/2}, it satisfies (2q - s^2) Delta_H(E) + 4(H ch_2^s(E))^2 - 6H^2 ch_1^s(E) ch_3^s(E) >= 0, where Delta_H(E) = (H^2 ch_1(E))^2 - 2(H^3 ch_0(E))(H ch_2(E)), ch_1^s(E) = ch_1(E) - sH ch_0(E), ch_2^s(E) = ch_2(E) - sH ch_1(E) + (s^2/2)H^2 ch_0(E), and ch_3^s(E) = ch_3(E) - sH ch_2(E) + (s^2/2)H^2 ch_1(E) - (s^3/6)H^3 ch_0(E)? ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s12215-022-00796-x.pdf))
justification: The draft is targeting Question 5.12, which appears in Section 5.3 immediately after the discussion of tilt stability, the classical Bogomolov inequality (5.4), and the generalized inequality (5.5). The surrounding paragraph explicitly says that, after the quintic and the (2,4) complete-intersection cases, the next Calabi-Yau complete-intersection case to address is the (3,2,2) complete intersection in P^6; the question is then stated almost verbatim. The main repairs are: replacing '(4.5)' by '(5.5)', and making explicit the polarization H, the notation sigma_{s,q}, the region Delta, and the definitions entering (5.5). The paper does not give an explicit equivalent reformulation of Question 5.12. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s12215-022-00796-x.pdf))
